blocks.value: Every Java application must include a class containing one `main` method. When you run a Java program, execution always begins there.
The method has two parts: the **heading** and the **body**.

items: `public static void main(String[] args)` is the heading.
The statements enclosed between the braces form the **body**, containing the declarations and execution of the program.

blocks.value: Every word in that heading is doing a job:

rows: An access modifier. The heading must be public so the Java interpreter can call it and run the class.
Means the method can be called without first creating an object of the class.
Indicates that `main` does not return any value when it is called.
The method name. The JVM always executes `main` first.
The type of argument that can be passed to `main`, an array of strings from the command line.

blocks.value: You will write this line in every program for a long time before you need to think about it. That is fine. Copy it now; `static` will make full sense in the Intermediate tier.
`String[] args` holds any words typed after the class name when the program is run. This program greets whoever is named on the command line:

Running `java Greet Ana` prints `Hello, Ana!`. If you run `java Greet` with no words, `args[0]` does not exist and the program stops with an error, which is a third kind of error described in Lesson 7.
